mattacatukka: [Matta3+catukka]  CL=7 Mattacatukka refers to the fourfold pārājika offenses related to a drunkard woman. Suppose an enemy brings a drunkard woman to monks and places her in such a way that her anus (vaccamagga) comes into contact with the monk’s genital organ. In that case, the monk incurs a pārājika offense if he experiences pleasure during the moments of insertion, penetration, placement, or withdrawal. Similarly, if the woman is positioned so that her genital area (passāvamagga) comes into contact with the monk’s genital organ, the same fourfold pārājika offense applies. Even if there is no pleasure during insertion, penetration, or placement, but there is pleasure at the moment of withdrawal, the pārājika offense still applies. These four aspects are called "catukka." When these fourfold offenses occur in threefold repetitions related to a drunkard woman, it is referred to as "mattacatukka."

mattikālepasaṅkhyā: [Mattikālepa+saṅkhyā] (thī) CL=7 The number of smearing with clay.
mattikāmakkhitasarīra: [Mattikāmakkhita+sarīra] (ti) CL=7 One whose body is applied with clay.
mattikāmaya: [Mattikā+maya] (ti) CL=7 Should be made with clay.
mattikāmayaghara: [Mattikāmaya+ghara] (na) CL=7 A house made of clay. See - Bhūrighara.
mattikāmayapatta: [Mattikāmaya+patta] (pu) CL=7 A bowl made of clay. An earthenware bowl. See - Mattikāpatta.
mattikāpiṇḍa: [Mattikā+piṇḍa] (pu) CL=7 A lump of earth. Mattikāpiṇḍa(pu) [mattikā+piṇḍa] a lump of earth.
mattikāpiṇḍaphala: [Mattikāpiṇḍa+phala] (na) CL=7 Benefits of donating a lump of earth.
mattikāpiṇḍaṭṭhapana: [Mattikāpiṇḍa+ṭhapana] (na) CL=7 Keeping the lump of soil.
mattikāpākāra: [Mattikāpākāra] (pu) CL=7 A wall made of clay.
mattikāratta: [Mattikā+ratta] (na) CL=7 Red soil. The soil"s color is like the dawn (light).
mattikārattuppalahāraka: [Mattikārattuppala+hāraka] (ti) CL=7 One who carries the lotus made of red clay.
mattikāsaññā: [Mattikā+saññā] (thī) CL=7 The perception that is earth.
mattikāthūpa: [Mattikā+thūpa] (pu,na) CL=7 A pagoda that is made of clay. An earthen pagoda.
mattisambhava: [Matti+sambhava] (ti) CL=7 One was born from a mother who is a Brahmin race.
mattākāra: [Matta3+ākāra] (pu) CL=7 The manner of drunkenness (or) intoxicated. See - Mattapamattākārapāpanaṭṭha.
mattāse: [Mattā(matta+yo)+se] (ti) CL=7 [See - Kuddhāse, Gatāse]. Those who are intoxicated.
mattāsukha: [Mattā1+sukha] (na) CL=7 Limited happiness (or) small comfort. See - Mattāsukhapariccāga.
mattāsukhapariccāga: [Mattāsukha+pariccāga] (pu) CL=7 Giving up a small comfort.
mattāvacana: [Mattā1+vacana] (na) CL=7 A word (sound) that is related to limitation. See - Mattāvacanānurūpa.
mattāvacanānurūpa: [Mattāvacana+anurūpa] (ti) CL=7 Suitable for the word (sound) that is related to limitation.
mattūpama: [Matta1+upamā] (ti) CL=7 A simile of a drunken person. Like a drunken person. One who is going as a drunken person.
matyā: [(ka)mātu+nā] (thī) CL=7 [Rū,nhā.90,91.(kha)mātu+smā. Nirutti,nhā.114] (A) Mother. (B) From mother.  matyā(thī) [mati+smā] From wisdom (or) knowledge.
matānusāra: [Mata+anusāra] (pu) CL=7 Following after a doctrine (or) belief.
matamanussamasa: [Matamanussa+maṃsa] (na) CL=7 The flesh of the dead person.
matamasa: [Mata+maṃsa] (na) CL=7 The meat of a deceased being. (in offering meat dishes to monks) meat not tainted with the stigma of being from an animal purposely killed for the occasion).
matirasi: [Mati+raṃsi] (thī) CL=7 The light of knowledge (or) wisdom.
matāṇa: [Amha+tāṇa] (ti) CL=7 [Moga,3.89. Nīti, sutta.543]  They have me (as their) protection.
